name: Sushi

cells.form: Hand-pressed nigiri, made in front of you
cells.rice: Red-vinegar rice; fish 'worked' — cured, simmered, marinated — not simply raw
cells.where: A counter; originally a street stall
cells.howToEat: A little soy on the fish side, one bite; set lunch at half the evening price

cells.form: Nigiri on plates, on a belt or ordered to your seat by screen
cells.rice: Machine-pressed; salmon is the most-ordered topping, 15 years running
cells.where: Suburban roadside and shopping malls; 4,000-plus shops
cells.howToEat: Pick or order, pay by the plate; ¥110–150 for the cheapest plate

lineages.name: Osaka box sushi
lineages.nameJa: 大阪の箱寿司・押し寿司

cells.form: Rice and fish pressed in a wooden box and cut; battera (mackerel)
cells.rice: Rice cooked with kelp stock and sweetened; fish marinated so no soy is needed
cells.where: A shop or a box to take away; the theatre interval meal
cells.howToEat: Without soy sauce; keeps for hours

cells.form: A round pressed cake of trout and rice in bamboo leaves
cells.where: Station kiosks and 20-plus specialist shops in Toyama city
cells.howToEat: Cut like a cake; eaten cold, hours later

cells.form: Whole crucian carp fermented in rice for months to years
cells.rice: The rice is a fermentation medium and was once discarded
cells.where: Festivals and homes around the lake; ¥5,400 for one fish
cells.howToEat: Sliced thin; pungent; the bones are soft enough to eat

cells.form: Salted mackerel on rice, wrapped in a persimmon leaf
A whole cured mackerel fillet pressed on rice, in kelp
Nigiri; 'conveyor' shops that take orders instead
cells.rice: Gas shrimp, sweet shrimp, nodoguro, white shrimp
cells.where: The city that spends most on sushi in Japan
cells.howToEat: Order from the counter, not the belt
